entries.title: Shared/Core update: free-agents
entries.summary: Shared/Core changes across 2 file(s) (+116/−16).

ai.title: Free tier agent exemption now requires specific model match
ai.summary: The free-tier small-request exemption for lightweight utility agents now requires both the agent ID and the specific model to match, replacing a simple agent-only check. This prevents arbitrary models from being charged zero credits when a lightweight helper like `file-picker` is running them. The change introduces `FREE_TIER_AGENT_MODELS` and `isFreeAgentModel` to enforce this model-level constraint, while updating documentation for daily session limits in the GPT-6.1 Sol promotion to clarify counting behavior.
ai.evidence: In `common/src/constants/free-agents.ts`, `FREE_TIER_AGENTS` is replaced by `FREE_TIER_AGENT_MODELS` and a new `isFreeAgentModel` helper is added that uses `matchesAllowedModel` to check the agent and model pair; `freebuff-sol-promo.ts` updates the JSDoc for `FREEBUFF_DAILY_SESSION_LIMITS` to explicitly exclude failed starts and fully refunded hours from the session count.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show if any legacy client bundles that rely on the old agent-only exemption will now start incurring minor credit charges for small requests.

eli5.text: The free-tier rule for small, automatic tasks (like quickly finding files) now checks both the task's name and the specific AI model doing the work. Previously, any model could perform these tiny tasks for free as long as the task had the right name; now, the model must also be on an approved list for that specific task. This change affects developers using the free tier who sometimes connect their own AI subscriptions; they will no longer see unexpected small charges when the assistant runs these quick helper tasks, provided the task uses an approved model. For most users, this is invisible maintenance that tightens billing accuracy; no action is needed, and existing sessions do not lose access.

ai.summary: The `common` package no longer defines the `PLATFORM_DAILY_STATS_BACKEND` constant or the `PlatformDailyStatsBackend` type, which previously gated whether the graphile job wrote daily stats to Postgres. The removal of the `platformDailyStatsWritesPostgres` helper indicates that the migration switch between the Convex cron and the Postgres mirror has been retired. This change consolidates the nightly engagement snapshot pipeline by eliminating the dual-write configuration logic.

ai.title: Add agentic offer training log provider constant
ai.summary: A new exported constant `AGENTIC_OFFER_TRAINING_LOG_PROVIDER` is defined in `common/src/ads/agentic-offer.ts` with the value `'agentic_offer'`. The comment states that this identifier names the `ad_provider_attempt.provider` field for decision rows in the ad training log, allowing a sponsored run to be joined back to the conversation via `proposal_id` and `campaign_id`. The constant is shared between the log producer and the reader in `@codebuff/bigquery/agentic-offer-context` to prevent the value from drifting. The diff contains only the definition and documentation; no code in the modified file or the visible diff references this constant as a runtime reader.
ai.evidence: The diff adds the export const AGENTIC_OFFER_TRAINING_LOG_PROVIDER = 'agentic_offer' to common/src/ads/agentic-offer.ts with a doc block citing @codebuff/bigquery/agentic-offer-context and COD-738.

ai.title: Add per-model tab limit function to desktop session constants
ai.summary: The shared `common` package now exports `freebuffDesktopModelTabLimit`, a utility that caps concurrent tabs on a single model based on its Freebucks price. The function returns 1 for free models (price 0) and Infinity for paid ones, reflecting that free models allow parallel agents at no cost. It accepts the price as a parameter because the CLI imports this module but cannot import the `freebuff-freebucks` package directly due to public export restrictions.
ai.evidence: The diff adds a new exported function `freebuffDesktopModelTabLimit` to `common/src/constants/freebuff-desktop-sessions.ts`, which returns 1 if the session price is 0 and Infinity otherwise, alongside existing desktop concurrency constants.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show which CLI components currently call this new function or how it interacts with existing concurrency limits.

eli5.text: A new decision rule is in place to cap how many parallel assistant windows you can open on a single AI model at once. For models that cost you nothing, the limit is one window; for models that cost Freebucks, there is no limit. This is internal plumbing for the desktop app and command-line interface, so nothing is live yet and you will not see any change in your daily use.

entries.title: Shared/Core update: billboard
entries.summary: Shared/Core changes across 1 file(s) (+10/−17).

ai.title: Simplify billboard ad frequency caps and drop refresh constants
ai.summary: The `common` package now enforces a single daily impression limit for both `Desktop-Billboard-Sidebar` and `Desktop-Billboard-Panel` ad slots, replacing the previous multi-tier caps and hourly rate limits. The sidebar slot frequency changed from 3 daily and 1 hourly impressions to a flat 1 daily impression, while the panel slot changed its attribution from individual ad units to the entire campaign. The now-unused constants `BILLBOARD_REFRESH_MS` and `BILLBOARD_PANEL_IDLE_MS` were removed, and the local `DAY_MS` helper was inlined without the `HOUR_MS` dependency.
ai.evidence: The diff in `common/src/ads/billboard.ts` changes `BILLBOARD_FREQUENCY_CAPS` to simplify the sidebar cap to a single daily limit and the panel cap to a campaign-level daily limit, while removing the exports `BILLBOARD_REFRESH_MS` and `BILLBOARD_PANEL_IDLE_MS` and updating the local `DAY_MS` constant definition.
ai.unknowns: The specific serving-engine implementation that now relies on 'Gravity' to release the screen, rather than a client-side refresh timer, is not visible in this diff.

eli5.text: The rules limiting how often full-screen billboards appear have been simplified so that an advertising campaign can now appear only once per day in the desktop sidebar and once per day in the side panel. Previously, the sidebar allowed up to three appearances per day with a limit of one per hour, but those extra tiers and the timers that triggered new ads were removed. This change affects advertisers buying space in the desktop app, not the people using the free coding assistant. You will notice slightly fewer repeated billboards, as the system now waits for a specific ad-serving process to release the screen instead of using a fixed refresh schedule.
